decisions.D-PCB-6: Under the GNSS line from the U3 RF pad (77.5, 29.1) to the J2 pin (86.96, 28.0), keep In1.Cu (GND plane) unbroken and keep tracks and vias off In1.Cu and In2.Cu in x 76..88, y 26.5..30.6 mm: a native rule area (no tracks, no vias, layers In1.Cu and In2.Cu) added to the board before routing. Basis: 50-ohm microstrip referenced to the In1 plane (RF_50 net class), reviewer condition on iteration 3. Applied at the next routing pass of iteration 3.
decisions.D-PCB-7: In1.Cu (GND) and In2.Cu (+3V3) are plane layers: native rule areas over the board outline with no-tracks on both layers (vias allowed, so fan-out and layer changes still pass through). Basis: the planed iteration-3 route placed signal tracks on In1.Cu (blocked-by top entries TIRE_CAN_TX_ENABLE, TWAI_RX, MCU_BOOT46, TWAI_TX on In1.Cu), which cuts the GND reference the RF_50 line and the bucks depend on (LMR36520 SNVSBF0C §8.5.1 item 5). Signal routing is F.Cu and B.Cu only; if two signal layers prove insufficient, the owner decision is a 6-layer stack, not tracks in the planes. Applied with D-PCB-6 before the next routing pass. REVISION v2 (2026-10-21): closing both inner layers starved routing (full pass on the D-PCB-3 board: 114 of 194 nets, versus 143-145 with four routable layers) and the kicad-route builtin engine ignored the inner-layer rule areas anyway (64 layer-change stubs placed inside them, reported to the kicad-route owner). Decision: In1.Cu stays a pure GND reference (no-tracks rule area over the outline; D-PCB-6 keeps vias out under the GNSS line); In2.Cu is opened to signal routing with the +3V3 pour filling around tracks (stack SIG / GND / PWR+SIG / SIG). If In2 routing still leaves power-distribution gaps, the owner decision is a 6-layer stack.
